thesis: Evidence-bounded thesis: A full-stack wheeled-base robot system for manufacturing and logistics, initially covering machine tending, tool setting, parts kitting and assembly, with remote human assistance. The reviewed public record does not independently establish a quantified customer problem. Verified current scope: workstation/cell; evidence level is stated in the claim ledger. Stated ambition: Walden states an ambition to combine full-stack robots, large behaviour models and remote assistance, beginning with production deployments in manufacturing and logistics. Public evidence supports responsibility for hardware, robot body, models/policies, simulation/training, integration, remote operations and hardware financing/RaaS; supports only partial/shared responsibility for end effectors/tooling and ongoing support/maintenance; does not establish responsibility for commissioning/qualification. Overall integration responsibility is classified as shared. Commercial evidence: 2_first_party_deployment_claim; technical evidence: 2_marketing_specific. These are public-evidence classifications, not proof of contract scope, uptime, economics or performance.
relevanceToIntegration: Partial integration comparator: public evidence supports a company role in integration or qualification, but responsibility is shared with a customer, OEM or partner. Commercial evidence is 2_first_party_deployment_claim; whole-workflow prime responsibility is not established.
evidenceGaps: Independent customer confirmation, contractual acceptance responsibility, deployment labour, uptime/SLA, pricing/revenue, repeat-deployment economics and current cap table remain unverified unless an atomic claim says otherwise.
